history.dynasty: Maratha (Chhatrapati Shahu Raje of Satara); Goud Saraswat Brahmin (GSB) community; spiritual guidance of Shrimad Swamiji of Shri Kavale Math
history.period: 1730–1738 (foundation to completion); original deity predates — moved in the 1560s
history.summary: Originally at Keloshi (Cavelossim), Salcette, where the temple was destroyed by the Portuguese in 1564–1566; the deity was carried via Cuncolim to Kavlem (then under the Bijapur Sultanate) and installed in a small laterite-mud shrine. At the request of Naroram Shenvi Rege (Naroram Mantri), a minister of Chhatrapati Shahu, the shrine was rebuilt — foundation laid 1730, completed 1738; Shahu Maharaja granted Kavalem village to the temple in 1739. The original murti was stolen by Pathans in 1898; a new murti was sculpted by Laxman Krishnaji Gaitonde and installed on 19 March 1902 (Phalgun Shukl Dashami, Shake 1823); the worn Shivalinga was replaced on 27 November 1965. CSV NOTE: 'Ponda' in the CSV is the taluka town ~3–4 km away; actual village is Kavalem (Ponda taluka, North Goa). POSSIBLE DUPLICATE: CSV row 225 (Shree Shantadurga Temple, Vasco da Gama) very likely describes this same famous temple; investigate and dedup. Distinct from CSV row 231 (Shree Shantadurga Fatarpekarin Temple), which is the separate Fatorpa temple.

name: Shri Shantadurga Temple
town_description: Kavalem is a small village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, at the foothill of a plateau about 30 km from Panaji. It is best known as the seat of the great Shantadurga temple, whose white-and-peach Indo-Portuguese complex dominates the village.

travel.railway: Margao Railway Station, about 20 km; Vasco da Gama about 34 km
travel.road: Kapileswari–Kavlem Road, Donshiwado, Ponda 403401; about 28–30 km from Panaji; easily combined with Mangueshi temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Magh (January–February) for the annual Jatrautsav
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM – 8:30 PM daily; no entry fee
